nodes.title: Dimitrov’s residual large-image theorem
nodes.statement: For a fixed non-CM regular cohomological Hilbert eigenform f, for all but finitely many rational primes ℓ and each relevant λ|ℓ, after conjugacy the residual image contains SL₂(F_q) for a finite subfield F_q⊆κ_λ, q=ℓ^a, and lies in κ_λ^×GL₂(F_q). In particular it contains a conjugate of SL₂(F_ℓ). Keep the finite exceptional set depending on f, its level, weights and coefficient field. Do not assert full GL₂(κ_λ).
hypotheses: Non-CM and k_τ≥2; finite bad set includes coefficient, weight and level exceptions.
Dimitrov’s integral/residual setup and coefficient embeddings are retained; the statement is uniform outside a finite set of rational characteristics.
proofSteps: Proposition 3.1 excludes residual reducibility outside a finite set using class field theory, labelled inertia and global units.
Proposition 3.5 excludes infinitely many dihedral images: finitely many quadratic fields/characters and congruences force a CM theta series.
§3.2 excludes exceptional projective images using tame-inertia orders as ℓ grows.
Apply Dickson’s classification to obtain Proposition 3.8 and the displayed subfield form.

sources.match: The three exclusions give the large residual subgroup.
The actual consumer passage invokes Dimitrov for the two residual images and simultaneous prime choice; it is not the proof of Proposition 5.4.

acceptance: For finitely many fixed forms, union their exceptional sets before choosing a common large ℓ.
A CM form has persistent dihedral projective image and is excluded.

nodes.title: Ribet–Momose large image for classical forms
nodes.statement: For a normalised non-CM classical cuspidal newform f of weight k≥2, the Zariski closure of ρ_f,λ contains SL₂ over the algebraic closure of K_f,λ for every λ. Its residual representation is absolutely irreducible for all but finitely many λ, and its residual image contains a conjugate of SL₂(F_ℓ) for all but finitely many rational ℓ, in particular for the large split primes used by Newton–Thorne. Inner twists may constrain the coefficient field and determinant: the open image is described using the inner-twist fixed field and its quaternion algebra, not automatically GL₂(O_K,λ).
hypotheses: Characteristic-zero statement holds for every λ; residual statement excludes a finite set.
Keep f fixed and non-CM.
proofSteps: Ribet 1985 §3 recalls Momose’s theorem: on the kernel of the inner twists the image is open in the reduced-norm-constrained unit group of a quaternion algebra over the fixed field.
After extending coefficients to an algebraic closure, its derived group gives SL₂.

Theorem 2.1 proves residual irreducibility and divisibility of image order by ℓ, using the conductors of twists (its Corollary 1.2, from local–global compatibility, R19.4/conductor-and-local-factors-classical) and the shape of the residual representation on inertia at ℓ (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.3); Theorem 3.1 upgrades this to the prescribed large image for almost all ℓ by finite-group classification and lifting commutators.

sources.match: Separates every-λ openness from almost-all residual image, with inner twists.
The actual prime-selection consumer asks for projective PSL₂ or PGL₂ image; Ribet 1985 is the primary large-image source.

acceptance: The theorem applies to Δ at every λ in characteristic zero; it makes no assertion about each small residual prime.
A CM theta series has torus-normaliser Zariski closure and fails the SL₂ conclusion.

nodes.title: Compatible family of a fixed eigenform
nodes.statement: For a fixed classical newform f, through π_f of infinity type (k, k − 2), or a fixed cuspidal π of infinity type (k,w) over a totally real F as in R19.2/all-cohomological-hilbert-representation, place the family {ρ_{π,λ}}_λ, indexed by the finite places λ of one coefficient field E ⊇ Q(π), in the early compatible-system carrier of R24.5:operations with: coefficient field E; ramification set S_π; good-place polynomials P_v(X) = X² − t_vX + q_vs_v ∈ E[X] for v ∉ S_π, independent of λ ∤ q_v; Hodge degrees (w − k_τ + 2)/2 and (w + k_τ)/2 at each τ; and at every finite v the Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne parameter ιRec_v(π_v ⊗ |·|_v^{−1/2}), for v ∤ ℓ by R19.4/all-hilbert-local-global-compatibility and for v | ℓ by R19.5/skinner-full-hilbert-coefficient-prime. The family is strictly compatible and pure of weight w + 1 at every finite place (R19.3/monodromy-weight-purity-of-the-family). With Kisin's theorem alone the coefficient-prime assertion is available at the λ with absolutely irreducible residual representation, and with Saito's alone under his degree and discrete-series hypotheses; a family known only by its good-place polynomials is weakly compatible.
hypotheses: Only regular weight k_τ ≥ 2 is in this family; finite-image weight-one systems use R19.1/weight-one-artin-representation.
One normalisation, ρ_{π,λ}, at every λ; Carayol's or Saito's family is σ_λ(π) = ρ_{π,λ} ⊗ χ_{π,λ}^{−1}, itself strictly compatible.
The carrier and the weak, almost strict and strict predicates belong to PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5:operations.
proofSteps: Construct each member by R19.2/all-cohomological-hilbert-representation; for F = Q identify it with M_{f,λ} (R19.1/newform-rank-two-realisation, dictionary (f)). No potential-modularity existence theorem is used.
Read the coefficients of P_v from the Hecke eigenvalues in E; attach the common WD parameters away from λ and at λ by the two compatibility theorems.
Compare Hodge data, determinants and coefficient changes; fill the imported predicates to the strength these inputs establish, and record purity from R19.3/monodromy-weight-purity-of-the-family.

Together the two local statements provide every finite place.

nodes.title: Full local–global compatibility away from the coefficient prime
nodes.statement: Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(A_F), F totally real of degree d, of infinity type (k,w): for every real place τ, π_τ is the discrete series D_{k_τ,w} with Blattner parameter k_τ and central character t ↦ sgn(t)^{k_τ}|t|^{−w} (Carayol 0.2–0.3; Skinner §1), with k_τ ≥ 2 and k_τ ≡ w mod 2 for all τ, including d even with π principal series at every finite place. For every finite place v ∤ ℓ: WD(ρ_{π,λ}|G_{F_v})^{F-ss} ≅ ιRec_v(π_v ⊗ |·|_v^{−1/2}) as Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations, including the monodromy operator (Skinner, equation (1)). In Carayol's normalisation this reads σ_λ(π)|W_{F_v} ≅ σ(π_v), Theorem (A) (R19.2/hilbert-normalisation-dictionary (a)). Consequently the Artin conductor of ρ_{π,λ} at v is a(π_v), L(WD(ρ_{π,λ}|G_{F_v}), s) = L(s − 1/2, π_v), and N ≠ 0 exactly when π_v is a twist of the Steinberg representation.
hypotheses: Frobenius-semisimplification keeps the Jordan form of N; agreement of traces or of semisimplified inertia alone is weaker.
Rec_v is normalised as in Skinner (uniformisers to geometric Frobenius), so the statement is about ρ_{π,λ}, not σ_λ(π).
proofSteps: Geometric case (d odd or a finite discrete-series place): Carayol's Theorem (A) (R19.2/hilbert-modular-compatible-system-carayol-theorem-A), including the extraordinary places in residue characteristic 2, which need cyclic and non-normal cubic base change (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4); translate by the dictionary.

Remaining case: the representation is Taylor's congruence construction, and the full compatibility at every v ∤ ℓ is the statement recalled by Skinner in (1) and by Blasius §2.3 and §3, with proofs by Taylor [Tay1, Tay2]; Taylor's original papers are a recorded source gap.

nodes.title: Kisin's coefficient-prime compatibility theorem
nodes.statement: Kisin's Theorem 4.3 in this roadmap's normalisation: let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(A_F), F totally real of degree d, of infinity type (k,w): for every real place τ, π_τ is the discrete series D_{k_τ,w} with Blattner parameter k_τ and central character t ↦ sgn(t)^{k_τ}|t|^{−w} (Carayol 0.2–0.3; Skinner §1), with k_τ ≥ 2 and k_τ ≡ w mod 2 for all τ, λ | p, and suppose the semisimplified reduction of ρ_{π,λ} is absolutely irreducible. Then for every place v | p of F, ρ_{π,λ}|G_{F_v} is potentially semistable with Hodge degrees (w − k_τ + 2)/2 and (w + k_τ)/2 at each τ, and the Frobenius-semisimplification of its Weil–Deligne representation (Fontaine's covariant D_pst, Kisin §4.2) is ιRec_v(π_v ⊗ |·|_v^{−1/2}), preserving N. Kisin's ρ_{π,λ} is defined by the geometric Frobenius polynomial X² − t_vX + N(v)s_v with positive-uniformiser operators, so it is ρ_{π,λ} itself, and the local Langlands correspondence of his Theorem 4.3 is the one fixed by (4.3.1), tr(w | σ_v) = t_v. No unramified-base, parallel-weight or discrete-series hypothesis is imposed. In the proof the fixed-type quotient and its period module exist over an arbitrary complete Noetherian local coefficient algebra A°.
hypotheses: Residual absolute irreducibility is essential to this route; R19.5/skinner-full-hilbert-coefficient-prime removes it.
The quotient property tests all finite Q_p-algebras, including algebras with nilpotents; field-valued points alone do not express it.
proofSteps: If π has a finite discrete-series place, apply Saito's comparison (R19.5/potential-semistability-and-compatibility-at-the-coefficient-prime) and translate by the dictionary.

Otherwise Taylor's auxiliary μ-new congruences modulo p^s for every s (R19.2/all-cohomological-hilbert-representation) have characteristic-zero points special at μ, which satisfy Saito's theorem and factor through the fixed crystalline Hodge-type quotient.
Apply Kisin's Theorems 2.5.5 and 2.7.6 for arbitrary A° (LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.3): the period module D_R with φ, and the trace T_φ of φ^{ν(w)} as a function on the quotient.
Congruences at every precision, closed quotient ideals and completeness give the factorisation R_{V_F} → T_m → O_{π,λ} through the quotient and T_φ ↦ t_v; Frobenius-semisimplification keeps N.

sources.match: Full arbitrary-totally-real theorem and congruence interpolation proof.
The quotient/period-family input is over arbitrary coefficient algebras.
Kisin's ρ_{π,λ} is the positive-uniformiser, geometric-Frobenius normalisation.

nodes.title: Skinner's full Hilbert coefficient-prime theorem
nodes.statement: Skinner's Theorem 1 in this roadmap's normalisation: let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL₂(A_F), F totally real of degree d, of infinity type (k,w): for every real place τ, π_τ is the discrete series D_{k_τ,w} with Blattner parameter k_τ and central character t ↦ sgn(t)^{k_τ}|t|^{−w} (Carayol 0.2–0.3; Skinner §1), with k_τ ≥ 2 and k_τ ≡ w mod 2 for all τ, λ | p, and v | p. Then ρ_{π,λ}|G_{F_v} is potentially semistable with Hodge degrees (w − k_τ + 2)/2 and (w + k_τ)/2 at each τ, and WD(ρ_{π,λ}|G_{F_v})^{F-ss} ≅ ιRec_v(π_v ⊗ |·|_v^{−1/2}) (Skinner (2)). Skinner's ρ_π is ρ_{π,λ} (his equation (1) and the trace identity of §2.4.2); his printed degrees (w − k_τ)/2 and (w + k_τ − 2)/2 are these under the shift of sourceIssue E4. No residual irreducibility and no discrete-series place is assumed.
hypotheses: Labelled degrees in the grading of the dictionary; the comparison is of full WD^{F-ss}, not only of Hodge numbers.
Generic period rings, D_pst and the Weil–Deligne functor are PadicHodgeTheory R06.3; this arithmetic theorem is owned here.
proofSteps: Known cases: Saito when d is odd or π has a finite discrete-series place (R19.5/potential-semistability-and-compatibility-at-the-coefficient-prime); Blasius–Rogawski when some k_τ > 2 and π is unramified above p (Skinner §2.3.2, through AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.1 and AG2.2 and PadicHodgeTheory R06.5); CM representations by Serre.

Reduction (Skinner §2.2): potential crystallinity and the trace identity (4) may be checked after an abelian base change F′/F with π_{F′} cuspidal and unramified above p (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4), because ρ_{π_{F′},λ} ≅ ρ_{π,λ}|G_{F′} (R19.2/hilbert-uniqueness-determinant-oddness-irreducibility); so assume d even, k_τ = 2, π principal series everywhere, unramified above p, not CM, and twist to w = 0.

Symmetric square (Skinner §2.4.1): by R19.2/hilbert-hodge-tate-property, ρ_v := ρ_{π,λ}|G_{F_v} is a quadratic twist of a crystalline representation, and the GL₃ realisation gives WD(Sym²ρ_v) ≅ ιRec_v(Sym²π_v ⊗ |·|_v^{−1}); hence WD(ρ_v) is a quadratic twist of ιRec_v(π_v ⊗ |·|_v^{−1/2}), and it suffices to show D_cris(ρ_v)^{φ^{f_v} = q_v^{1/2}α_v(ϖ_v)} ≠ 0 for π_v = π(α_v, β_v).

Family (Skinner §2.4.2): with D the totally definite quaternion algebra over F and Buzzard's overconvergent forms S^D_κ(U; m) over a weight disc B_r, a T^S-stable finite slope summand N gives a reduced affinoid A, φ: T^S → A and ρ_A on M = A ⊕ C (PadicFamilies L2a and L2, with Jacquet–Langlands GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.3); the specialisations at the dense set of classical points x, of infinity type ((n_x + 2)_τ, n_x) in this roadmap's normalisation (the source writes ((n_x + 2), n_x + 2), source issue E4), are ρ_{π_x,λ}, using their irreducibility (R19.2/hilbert-uniqueness-determinant-oddness-irreducibility).

Analytic continuation: Theorem 1 holds at those points by the Blasius–Rogawski case, so D_cris(ρ_x|D_v)^{φ^{f_v} = x(φ_v)} has rank ≥ 1; Kisin's analytic continuation of crystalline periods [Ki2, (5.14)–(5.15)], extended from G_{Q_p} to G_{F_v} as in Skinner's footnote 9 (PadicHodgeTheory R06.3), gives the same at x₀, which removes the quadratic ambiguity.

nodes.title: Ordinary refinement and saturated lattice
nodes.statement: For a classical weight-k newform with p∤N, k≥2 and a_p a λ-adic unit, fix the unit Euler root α of X²−a_pX+ε(p)p^{k−1}. The imported R21.3 ordinary theorem supplies 0→V⁺→ρ_f,λ→V⁻→0, with V⁻ unramified and arithmetic Frobenius acting by α, and V⁺ character ε·χ_p^{k−1}·(V⁻)⁻¹. For a fixed stable lattice T, define T⁺=T∩V⁺ and T⁻=T/T⁺. Prove T⁺ saturated, T⁻ torsion-free of rank one, and compatibility with the chosen unit-root refinement and with the modular-symbol period line. For Hilbert forms import the labelled ordinary characters from R21.3 rather than applying this Q-formula to every multiweight.
hypotheses: Good p and ordinary unit root; the other root has valuation k−1.
The stable lattice and rational period lines are already fixed; this construction does not canonically normalise a numerical period.

The lattice T is a stable lattice in the arithmetic ρ_{f,λ}, for instance the O_λ-dual of the integral realisation of R19.1/integral-structure-of-the-newform-premotive, twisted as in R19.1/newform-rank-two-realisation. On the cohomological M_{f,λ} the ordinary line is the unramified subrepresentation on which geometric Frobenius acts by α, and T⁺ is the annihilator of its saturation.
proofSteps: Import the ordinary exact sequence and character formulas from R21.3.
Intersect the invariant line with T. If a nonzero O_λ-scalar times t lies in the line, then t lies there, proving saturation.
The quotient is rank one and torsion-free over the DVR. Compare its unramified character with the unit root and transport the imported period line through the fixed realisation.

nodes.title: Nonordinary crystalline and Wach realisation
nodes.statement: For p∤N and any classical k≥2, identify D_cris of the cohomological eigenform realisation M_f,λ with its crystalline projector factor, with Hodge filtration in degrees 0,k−1 and φ-polynomial X²−a_pX+ε(p)p^{k−1}. For a fixed lattice, import P7’s Wach module in its admissible weight convention, with the dual/Tate twist recorded when required. Identify (N(T)/π)[1/p] with D_cris(T[1/p]) in that convention; N(T)/π itself is an integral O_λ-lattice. Transport φ and the filtration. A basis gives a semilinear Wach Frobenius matrix; basis change acts by U⁻¹Pφ(U), so this matrix is not canonical. The two Euler roots used by signed regulators are roots of this polynomial after coefficient extension. If they repeat, do not claim two independent eigenlines or invert their difference.
hypotheses: Good reduction; no ordinarity assumption. A signed regulator itself belongs to its Iwasawa owner.
Fix the P7 Wach weight convention and explicit dual/twist before comparing to M; no Fontaine–Laffaille bound is imposed on crystalline existence.
A diagonalisation/eigenline comparison requires distinct roots and a splitting coefficient extension.

Import the integral Wach module of T and the rational P7 comparison (N(T)/π)[1/p]≅D_cris(T[1/p]), retaining the dual/twist weight convention and semilinearity.
Compute φ on the factor from geometric Frobenius/Hecke comparison; compare Euler roots, coefficient extension and lattice reduction.

nodes.title: Endpoint-weight local contract
nodes.statement: For a good-prime classical eigenform of weight k=p+1, the coefficient-prime theorem still gives a crystalline characteristic-zero representation with arithmetic Hodge weights {0,p} and its full local parameter. The integral Fontaine–Laffaille comparison used for the chosen parabolic lattice requires [0,k−1]⊆[0,p−2] and therefore does not apply. Weight p+1 alone does not imply that this representation is Barsotti–Tate or that its residual inertial type has a prescribed ordinary/flat lift. Any such lifting conclusion must specify a different weight-two potentially Barsotti–Tate lift, a residual weight/type comparison and its hypotheses from R07/R20/R21; no endpoint conclusion is read off a_p alone.
hypotheses: p∤N; ordinary refinements additionally require a_p a unit.
Keep characteristic-zero Hodge type, residual Serre weight and the type of a chosen deformation lift distinct.
proofSteps: Apply the general good-prime crystalline theorem, which has no Fontaine–Laffaille range restriction.
Compute k−1=p>p−2 to exclude the chosen integral comparison.
Import endpoint residual weight/type comparison only with its explicit theorem hypotheses; record the missing converse/lifting input instead of promoting the integral comparison.

nodes.title: Ordinary CM primes split
nodes.statement: For a regular cohomological CM Hilbert form f=AI_L^F(α) that is p-ordinary at every v|p, each v|p splits in the CM quadratic extension L/F, and the inducing character has a p-ordinary CM type compatible with the chosen embeddings. For the Hara–Ochiai converse retain the source’s p-ordinary CM-type/infinity-type hypothesis; splitting alone without that hypothesis is not the stated iff criterion.
hypotheses: CM is a hypothesis of Hara–Ochiai Proposition A.3; the theorem is not for arbitrary ordinary Hilbert forms.
Regular weights make the two inducing local characters distinct; arbitrary index-two induction need not be locally irreducible.
proofSteps: At a nonsplit v, restrict the induced representation to G_Fv; regular labelled Hodge types distinguish α from its local conjugate, so induction is irreducible.
The R21.3 ordinary triangular theorem makes that local representation reducible, a contradiction.
Use the valuation/infinity-type calculation in Hara–Ochiai to identify the p-ordinary CM type and the converse under its full hypotheses.

Since v splits, G_Fv⊂G_L. With distinct ordinary local characters, the ordinary line is one of the two global G_L-character lines, and τ interchanges them.

An arbitrary invariant line when the two local characters coincide does not satisfy this argument.

nodes.title: Hyodo–Kato and de Rham automorphic multiplicities
nodes.statement: In CDN §5.2.1 let F/Q_p be finite, E totally real with E_𝔭=F, B̌/E ramified at 𝔭 and split at exactly one real place, and B its inner form split at 𝔭 and compact at infinity, with the other local invariants as in the source. Let M∈ΦN^ϖ be a two-dimensional supercuspidal (φ,N,G_F)-module over L with ϖ acting trivially on JL(M), choose n such that JL(M) is trivial on 1+ϖ_D^n O_D, and take Π̌∈SD_{2,n} defined over L with Π̌_𝔭=JL(M). Here SD₂ imposes the holomorphic discrete-series representation of weight two and trivial central character at the distinguished real place ∞₀, and the trivial representation at every other real place; a globally trivial central character is not assumed. Write Π_f^p=Π̌_f^p and Sh_n for the quaternionic Shimura-curve tower. Then Hom_{Ǧ(A_f^p)}(Π_f^p,L⊗Q_p H_HK¹(Sh_n))≅JL(M)⊗_L M. For F⊆K, Hom_{Ǧ(A_f^p)}(Π_f^p,L⊗Q_p H_dR¹(Sh_n,K))≅JL(M)⊗_L(K⊗_F M_dR). The isomorphisms respect the period structures, local group action and comparison map with the source’s coefficient completions.
hypotheses: Retain the globalisation, ϖ-compatibility, level n, weight-two archimedean type, supercuspidal parameter and coefficient-field hypotheses. Globalisation can require a character twist and a finite extension of L (CDN footnote 21). For de Rham cohomology K contains E and F via the fixed embedding E→E_𝔭=F→K.
This is an automorphic multiplicity extraction, not a claim about the entire cohomology or a new local p-adic Langlands construction.

CDN's ρ_Π satisfies H¹_ét = ⊕ Π_f ⊗ ρ_Π(−1); the multiplicity space is Carayol's σ_λ for his action of the adelic group on cohomology (his 2.3), so ρ_Π = ρ_{π,λ}^∨ for the Jacquet–Langlands transfer π (R19.2/hilbert-normalisation-dictionary (h)). The source normalises its local correspondence so that the central character corresponds to the determinant divided by the cyclotomic character, which is the Tate-module normalisation and agrees with this.
proofSteps: Decompose étale cohomology of the curve tower as ⊕_π π_f⊗ρ_π(−1) in CDN’s convention.
Use full local compatibility at every finite place, including 𝔭, to identify D_pst(ρ_Π̌,𝔭(−1)) with M.
Apply generic semistable/de Rham comparison and then the away-p Hom functor; strong multiplicity one says Π_f^p determines Π_𝔭.
Use D_dR to obtain the second identity and its comparison compatibility.

nodes.title: Density-one ordinary primes in weight two
nodes.statement: For the non-CM weight-two newform f of squarefree level N and trivial nebentypus in Skinner 2020 §3, the rational primes p∤N for which f is ordinary at some λ|p have density one. For all sufficiently large such p, every λ|p has absolutely irreducible residual representation, and that residual representation is ramified at every q|N. Thus one may choose p≥5 and λ|p ordinary while retaining all these residual conditions. The quantifier for ordinarity is some λ, while the eventual irreducibility/ramification statements hold for every λ.
hypotheses: Fixed non-CM weight-two form; retain squarefree N and trivial character for this routed level-lowering argument.
Exclude finitely many coefficient ramification and small primes.

Use Ribet 1985 Theorem 2.1 for eventual residual absolute irreducibility.

If residual ramification at q|N failed for infinitely many large p, R20.2 level lowering and finiteness of weight-two lower-level forms produce one g congruent to f in infinitely many characteristics. Its good coefficients equal those of f; multiplicity one contradicts its lower conductor.

nodes.title: Geometric determinant over the integral Hecke algebra
nodes.statement: Let O be a complete coefficient DVR and T_m the completed local finite O-flat Hecke algebra of the fixed classical/Hilbert geometric eigensystem, allowing nilpotents. Extract from cohomology a faithful continuous generic rank-two T_m[1/p]-module with G_{F,S}-action commuting with T_m, retaining generalised oldform eigenspaces where present. Its determinant polynomial law descends to a continuous degree-two law D:T_m[G_{F,S}]→T_m: the good-prime coefficients are T_v and Nv S_v in the geometric-Frobenius convention, and all finite-quotient specialisations have the induced law. This descent retains the entire integral ring, not merely its reduced eigenform points. For torsion/non-flat Hecke settings the missing integral cohomological determinant construction is explicitly a gap, not an inference from field-valued points.
hypotheses: T_m is O-flat, so T_m→T_m[1/p] is injective even if T_m is nonreduced.
The generic rank-two module is supplied by the geometric multiplicity-space construction, not reconstructed from reduced points.
The arithmetic-dual convention must be translated before using a universal arithmetic deformation problem.

In weight two the module is the cohomology H¹ of the modular curve, the dual of Darmon–Diamond–Taylor's V = T_ℓ(J) ⊗ Q_ℓ: on V an arithmetic Frobenius has polynomial X² − T_pX + p⟨p⟩, and the law here has those coefficients at geometric Frobenius. Its residual law is that of the dual of the arithmetic residual representation.
proofSteps: Use the Hecke-equivariant parabolic/Jacobian/Shimura-curve cohomology and its multiplicity-space decomposition to obtain the generic rank-two family over the actual Hecke algebra.
Good-prime trace and determinant lie in T_m. Density of good Frobenius and continuity place these coefficients at every group element in the closed integral algebra.

Import IHG.4’s integral rank-two law descent: for Σ a_i g_i its diagonal coefficients are det(g_i) and its cross coefficient at a_i a_j is tr(g_i)tr(g_j)−tr(g_i g_j). Thus no division by 2 is required.
Injectivity into T_m[1/p] transfers all polynomial-law identities; finite quotients give continuity and retain nilpotents.

sources.locator: §4.1, the structure of the full Hecke algebra, pp. 109–110, and Lemmas 1.37–1.39
sources.match: Supplies a generic rank-two Hecke module even when the old Hecke algebra is nonreduced.
The integral Hecke family and its finite-precision quotients are used geometrically.

Distinct laws over k[ε]/ε² can have identical k-valued specialisations.

api.statement: The integral degree-two law from the actual geometric generic rank-two Hecke family.

api.name: TauCeti.ModularGalois.geometricHeckeDeterminant_goodFrob
api.statement: Its characteristic polynomial at good geometric Frobenius has coefficients T_v,Nv S_v.

api.name: TauCeti.ModularGalois.geometricHeckeDeterminant_continuous
api.statement: Compatible continuous laws over all finite quotients T_m/m^n.

api.name: TauCeti.ModularGalois.geometricHeckeDeterminant_coeffChange
api.statement: Coefficient quotient/extension commutes with the geometric determinant.

api.name: TauCeti.ModularGalois.geometricHeckeDeterminant_residual
api.statement: Reduction identifies with det ρ̄ of the residual eigensystem, ρ̄ being taken in the geometric convention (the dual of the arithmetic residual representation).

api.name: TauCeti.ModularGalois.geometricHeckeDeterminant_wholeRing
api.statement: All identities hold over T_m, including its nilpotents, rather than only T_m,red.

tests.name: TauCeti.ModularGalois.geometricHeckeDeterminant_dualNumbers
tests.statement: Over A=k[ε]/ε², diag(1+ε,1) and identity have the same reduced point but different determinant at the generator of an infinite cyclic group.

tests.name: TauCeti.ModularGalois.geometricHeckeDeterminant_finiteQuotients
tests.statement: Reduction from T_m/m^{n+1} to T_m/m^n agrees with the n-th law.

tests.name: TauCeti.ModularGalois.geometricHeckeDeterminant_characteristicTwo
tests.statement: The cross coefficient tr(g)tr(h)−tr(gh) is integral in characteristic two; no 1/2 formula is used.

tests.name: TauCeti.ModularGalois.geometricHeckeDeterminant_oldspace
tests.statement: Retain the nonzero nilpotent u(u²+2u+2) in the level-88 old Hecke factor instead of replacing that factor by its reduced quotient.

uses.how: Supply the integral continuous law before applying residual reconstruction.
Provide complete local Hecke families and finite-precision specialisations.

nodes.title: Local conditions of the integral Hecke family
nodes.statement: For the reconstructed continuous Hecke-algebra representation with specified absolutely irreducible residual representation, prove determinant and ramification conditions over T_m and all finite quotients. For a chosen deformation condition at each v, verify factorisation through its representing local quotient (fixed determinant, minimal/unramified, ordinary flagged, or potentially semistable with specified Hodge/inertial type) and hence construct the map from the global universal deformation ring. Verification at characteristic-zero eigenform fields alone proves the condition only on the reduced generic fibre. For an O-flat family, a defining ideal vanishing over the whole generic algebra, including its nilpotents, vanishes integrally; use finite-algebra period-family or geometric flagged conditions to establish that premise. Integral flat/ordinary conditions at torsion quotients require their exact deformation-functor argument.
hypotheses: Local conditions are specified functors/quotients, not the open assertion N≠0 at every Artinian point.
An ordinary condition may require a chosen invariant saturated line and character; traces alone do not choose a flag.
Do not assume Artinian quotients of T_m embed into products of eigenform field quotients.
proofSteps: Good-prime polynomial identities and G_{F,S}-factorisation give determinant and unramified-outside-S conditions at all finite quotients.
Use geometric invariant lines for ordinary local conditions, and Kisin’s finite-algebra period-family quotient for fixed potentially semistable/Hodge/inertial type.
Verify annihilation of each local-condition ideal on the actual generic algebra and use O-flatness to descend, or prove the integral finite-quotient condition directly.
Apply R04’s representing property to get R→T_m. Record the DDT type-Σ exercise and non-flat extensions as proof gaps until their local functor arguments are supplied.

sources.match: Construction is proved, but the remaining type-Σ checks must not be silently declared solved.
Use conditions on finite coefficient algebras, not just dense field points.

acceptance: T_m/m^n has the specified determinant for every n.
A local-condition equation equal to a nonzero nilpotent is invisible at every field point and obstructs factorisation.

requests.need: Betti, de Rham (with Hodge filtration) and étale parabolic cohomology of the modular curves with coefficients in Sym^{k−2} of the relative H^1 of the universal elliptic curve, with comparison isomorphisms, Poincaré duality and change-of-level compatibility (as used by Diamond–Flach–Guo §§2–3); and their S-integral versions for S ⊇ {ℓ | Nk!}, with Faltings' crystalline realisation and the integral q-expansion principle (Diamond–Flach–Guo §§1.2, 2, Lemma 4.12). Additional interface: Universal elliptic family, Sym^r coefficient sheaf, parabolic cohomology and level/Hecke pull–push comparison with Kuga–Sato cohomology. Additional interface: Eichler–Shimura comparison with coefficients, rational new Hecke factor, coefficient-field action and Betti/de Rham/étale realisations with the modular-symbol period lines; exact descent in Scholl/DFG normalisations.
Tate modules of abelian varieties as continuous G_Q-modules, with their K_f-action for A_f, and smooth proper base change for good reduction.

Existence of G-stable lattices in continuous ℓ-adic representations of compact groups and Brauer–Nesbitt independence of the semisimplified reduction; Čebotarev uniqueness of semisimple representations with given Frobenius traces. Additional interface: Dirichlet characters as finite-order G_Q characters through Gal(Q(ζ_N)/Q), arithmetic good Frobenius value χ(q), and the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character of good Frobenius value q; used for the Eisenstein direct sum. Additional interface: For a complete DVR with finite residue field of characteristic ℓ, reduction GL_n(O/π^(m+1))→GL_n(O/π^m) is surjective; its successive congruence kernels are additive matrix ℓ-groups, and GL_n(O) is the topological inverse limit of these groups. Residual recognition in characteristic ℓ uses full characteristic polynomials, not traces alone. Additional interface: Stable lattices and lattice-independent residual semisimplification of the Hilbert eigenform representations, followed by full-polynomial recognition over the residue field; the classical-newform residual node is not this Hilbert input.

Weil–Deligne representations of local Weil groups with Deligne's normalisation F N F^{−1} = q^{−1}N for geometric Frobenius, Frobenius-semisimplification and Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem. Additional interface: Purity of Weil–Deligne representations in the monodromy sense (Deligne): q-Weil numbers, the classification of Frobenius-semisimple indecomposables Λ ⊗ V_t, and stability of purity under sums, duals, Tate twists and tensor products (Blasius §§1.8–1.10, Proposition 1).

Local Langlands for GL_2(Q_p) and GL_2(F_v) with the Hecke normalisation σ_h (Carayol 0.5) and its relation to Langlands' (twist by ω^{1/2}, contragredient); preservation of conductors, L- and ε-factors; unramified twists of Steinberg ↔ N ≠ 0. Additional interface: Twisting and duality for the Langlands parameter: Rec_v(π_v ⊗ (χ∘det)) = Rec_v(π_v) ⊗ Rec_v(χ), Rec_v(π_v^∨) = Rec_v(π_v)^∨, π_v^∨ ≅ π_v ⊗ χ_{π_v}^{−1} for GL₂, and preservation of L-, ε-factors and conductors under these operations.

Shimura curves attached to quaternion algebras over totally real fields split at one real place, with the ℓ-adic sheaves F_λ and the Hecke decomposition of their cohomology used by Carayol (§§1–10). Additional interface: The CDN §5.2.1 quaternionic Shimura-curve tower and automorphic decomposition of H¹ with π_f⊗ρ_π(−1), all group actions and direct limits; HK/de Rham multiplicity extraction is owned here. Additional interface: Faithful generic rank-two Hecke multiplicity module from geometric cohomology, including the completed local algebra’s generalised eigenspaces, coefficient change and topology; needed before law descent. Additional interface: Quaternionic Shimura surfaces Sh_B for B split at exactly two real places and at every finite place, and Blasius's Proposition 6 (Reimann's Hasse–Weil zeta computation; Brylinski–Labesse for intersection cohomology when B = M₂): the constituents of H²(Sh_{B,W}, Q_ℓ)(π′_f) over Γ_L are those of ρ_{π,λ}|_L ⊗ ^{τ₂}ρ_{π,λ}|_L. Also the Hecke algebras with level at an auxiliary prime μ and their μ-new quotients used in Taylor's congruences (Kisin §4.3).
Carayol's integral models of Shimura curves and their bad reduction (Compositio 59, 1986), on which Theorem (B) depends.

The generic compatible-system carrier with weak, almost-strict and strict local predicates (Dieulefait–Pacetti Definition 1.10 after Khare–Wintenberger). Additional interface: Early compatible-system carrier over a number field, coefficient extension/dual/twist operations and explicit weak/almost-strict/strict predicates. This import precedes R24 potential-modularity existence, avoiding a cycle. Additional interface: The strict predicate filled by the fixed eigenform family and the purity field it records.

Purity for the eigenform/Kuga–Sato eigenspace with its projector hypotheses (Ramanujan–Petersson in the geometric form). Additional interface: Purity and monodromy-weight theorem for the parabolic/Kuga–Sato and Shimura-curve coefficient realisations, including Saito’s required vanishing input, and preservation under eigenform projectors and coefficient extension. Additional interface: Its hilbert-local-monodromy-weight-export node is only the Saito geometric case (g>1,w≥k_τ≥2 and a finite discrete-series place in even degree). Request the vanishing/projector transport in that scope; full all-Hilbert purity requires a separate precise proof input. Do not treat an export depending on the retired R06.6 modular application as an independent generic supplier. Saito's weight theorem stated on the geometric realisations: for the semistable model of R34.3/saito-semistable-comparison-model, the monodromy filtrations of the ℓ-adic eigensummand H¹(M, F(k)) and of its log-crystalline (Hyodo–Kato) realisation are pure of weight w_S − 1 (Saito §8 and Proposition 1, §10). It must not import the coefficient-prime theorem of R19.5 or the retired PadicHodgeTheory R06.6 application, which R19.5 owns.

Mod-ℓ modular forms: the Eisenstein weight shift and the lifting of mod-λ eigenvalues (Deligne–Serre 6.9–6.11). Additional interface: Deligne–Serre 6.7 includes noncuspidal forms and coefficient characteristic dividing the level. The existing reduction-to-weight-at-least-two node assumes a cuspidal integral reduction and ℓ prime to level; retain it for that subset and supply the general Eisenstein weight-shift/reduction-image argument and its integrality hypotheses for 6.7. The existing eigenvalue-lifting lemma remains the exact finite-free commuting-Hecke input.

Chenevier Theorem 2.22(i): faithful Cayley–Hamilton quotient over a henselian local coefficient ring with residually split absolutely irreducible determinant is M₂(A); reconstruction, conjugacy/strict equivalence and continuity. No algebraically-closed-residue hypothesis and no Deligne–Serre lifting step. Additional interface: Characteristic-zero continuous semisimple reconstruction of the compatible Taylor trace/determinant, without assuming that the residual representation at every λ is absolutely irreducible. Additional interface: Pseudo-character reconstruction of a continuous semisimple representation from compatible traces and determinants modulo λ^s (Taylor's congruence branch).

The Jacquet–Langlands correspondence between automorphic representations of (D ⊗ A_F)^× and cuspidal representations of GL_2(A_F) that are discrete series at the ramification places of D, with local functoriality at every place (one-dimensional representations of D_v^× ↔ unramified twists of Steinberg), as used by KW II §7 and Taylor. Additional interface: Jacquet–Langlands to the totally definite quaternion algebra split at all finite places (Skinner §2.4.2), matching T^S-eigensystems.

The weight-two Hecke algebra 𝕋_ℤ of Γ_H(N) generated by the T_n and ⟨d⟩, acting on J_Γ and T_ℓ(J_Γ) compatibly with G_ℚ; faithfulness on S₂(Γ, R) and finite freeness of 𝕋_R; the Weil-pairing adjointness of T and w_N T w_N; and H₁(X_Γ, ℤ) ⊗ ℚ free of rank two over 𝕋_ℚ (Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Lemmas 1.34–1.39).

The universal deformation ring R_Σ of liftings of type Σ of an odd absolutely irreducible ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(k), ℓ odd (determinant ε, the flat, ordinary or semistable condition at ℓ, minimal ramification at p ∉ Σ, no condition at p ∈ Σ − {ℓ}), with its universal representation ρ^univ_Σ, and the stability of these local conditions under products, subobjects and quotients. Additional interface: Representability and coefficient-quotient stability of the specified fixed-determinant/minimal/ordinary/flat type-Σ local functors and their global universal ring; supply the DDT Lemma 3.27 finite-quotient argument without a false product-embedding assumption. Additional interface: For the Hilbert non-Eisenstein residual representation, the universal fixed determinant ψχ_p deformation functor unramified outside S (and with every local condition explicitly named when one is imposed). Check the Schur and finite-generation hypotheses of R04.2 before invoking the universal ring.

Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Theorem 3.15 (Diamond's weight-two level optimisation): for ℓ odd and ρ̄ absolutely irreducible and modular (with ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(√−3)}} absolutely irreducible if ℓ = 3), a weight-two newform f with ρ̄_f ≅ ρ̄, N_f = N(ρ̄)ℓ^{δ(ρ̄)} and ψ_f of order prime to ℓ. Additional interface: Endpoint residual weight p+1 versus existence of a weight-two potentially Barsotti–Tate/ordinary lift, with every irreducibility and local-type hypothesis. Do not infer this from crystalline weight p+1 alone.

Generation of the weight-two Hecke algebra 𝕋_R of Γ_H(N) (Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Lemma 4.1): by the T_n, or by the T_p and ⟨d⟩; and, for D prime to N with D odd or 2 invertible in R, by the T_n with (n, D) = 1 (Diamond–Im Proposition 3.5.1; Wiles 1995, p. 491).

The newform decomposition S₂(Γ_H(N), K) = ⊕_f S_{K,f} over newforms f of level N_f | N, with S_{K,f} spanned by the f(aτ), a | N/N_f (Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Theorem 1.22), and the characteristic polynomial u^{v−1}(u² − a_p(f)u + ψ_f(p)p) of T_p on the span of the f(ap^iτ), v = v_p(N/N_f). For Deligne–Serre 5.2, in any weight k: an eigenform of the T_p, p ∤ N, has the eigenvalues of a newform of level dividing N (Atkin–Lehner–Li), whose coefficients are multiplicative with a_{p^m} = a_p^m and |a_p| < p^{k/2} at p | N.

The supersingular locus of Carayol's Shimura curves at 𝔭 ≠ v through Drinfeld's formal 𝒪_𝔭-modules of height 2 with level structure (Carayol §§7–9: the formalism, the universal deformation with level structure, and the supersingular orbit revisited), and Brylinski's appendix identifying the vanishing cycles with the cohomology of the generic fibre of the completed strict henselisation. These give the local fundamental representation 𝒰 of W(F̄_𝔭/F_𝔭) × GL₂(F_𝔭) × B̄_𝔭^× (10.3).

The vanishing-cycle exact sequence for a proper curve over a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring with a lisse coefficient sheaf, and its compatibility with finite étale covers and group actions, as Carayol uses it in 4.2–4.5.

Picard–Lefschetz for a stable curve X over a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring (after the Deligne–Mumford semistable reduction theorem): the monodromy logarithm N maps H¹(X_η̄, F)(1) onto ker(H¹(X_s, F) → H¹(X̃_s, F)), the kernel of pull-back to the normalisation X̃_s, for a lisse F (Carayol 11.4–11.10, Langlands [L.1] for F = ℚ).

Local and global base change for GL₂ along extensions of degree at most 3: Langlands for cyclic extensions and Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika for non-Galois cubic ones, with the compatibility of the lift with restriction of the Weil–Deligne representation for principal series, special and ordinary cuspidal π, which Carayol (12.2.2) asserts without a reference. Additional interface: Cyclic totally real base change, descent and compatibility of attached good-prime polynomials with restriction; do not infer non-normal cubic base change from cyclic base change. Additional interface: Cyclic and non-normal cubic base change with local parameters and compatibility with Galois restriction, including Carayol §12.2.2; cyclic base change alone does not supply the cubic step. Additional interface: The existing nonnormal-cubic-base-change node supplies only almost-all Satake compatibility. Carayol §12.2.1–12.2.2 requires the stronger local parameter/restriction assertion for principal series, special and ordinary cuspidal components at the chosen place; retain this as an additional request/gap, not an implication of weak transfer. Additional interface: Abelian (cyclic, solvable) base change of a cuspidal π of infinity type (k,w) to a totally real F′, cuspidal unless π is induced from F′, compatible with Satake parameters at unramified places and with Rec at every place; totally real quadratic base change; and the Gelbart–Jacquet lift Sym²π ⊗ |·|^{−1} to GL₃, cuspidal for non-CM π.

Automorphic induction 𝒲(L, ξ) from a CM quadratic extension L/F with prescribed local component, archimedean types and behaviour at v (Carayol 11.2); Tunnell's globalisation of primitive local representations ([Tu. 1], Theorem 1.3); and the Artin conjecture for tetrahedral (Langlands) and octahedral (Tunnell) representations, with Jacquet–Langlands chapter 12. Additional interface: Algebraic Hecke-character automorphic induction for quadratic extensions, theta-series correspondence, nontrivial quadratic self-twist criterion and index-two induced representation dictionary. Additional interface: The Grunwald–Wang existence theorem in the form Blasius §2.2 uses: for a totally real F, a finite place v and a finite-order character ψ of F_v^×, a finite-order idele class character η of F with η_v = ψ. The node R17.5/finite-hecke-extension treats the related extension problem for characters of roots of unity.

Dickson's classification for subgroups G of GL₂(F_ℓ) whose identity representation is semisimple, in the form of Serre, Propriétés galoisiennes des points d'ordre fini des courbes elliptiques (Invent. Math. 15, 1972), §2, Propositions 15–16, as Deligne–Serre 7.2 use it: G contains SL₂(F_ℓ), or lies in a Cartan subgroup, or lies in the normaliser of a Cartan subgroup but not in it, or has projective image A₄, S₄ or A₅. The reducible (diagonalisable) case is included. Additional interface: Continuous finite-dimensional Clifford theory and Ribet 1975 Theorem 2.3 for compact semisimple λ-adic groups with an open abelian subgroup and infinite projective image. Additional interface: Dickson classification with subfield form, exceptional-group bounds and tame-inertia order argument; generic finite/Lie-group input only, the non-CM Hilbert application is owned here. Additional interface: Generic compact λ-adic Lie-group Zariski closure, quaternionic norm-one groups, finite-group classification and integral commutator lifting. The modular inner-twist/Momose application remains owned by R19.3.

Čebotarev recognition in characteristic zero for representations of G_ℚ with finite image (Deligne–Serre Lemme 3.2), after realising both over a common field; coefficient descent over a finite field (Lemme 6.13); and the fact that every element of a finite image of G_ℚ is a Frobenius at a prime outside any given finite set. Additional interface: Čebotarev/Brauer–Nesbitt recognition and continuous rank-two pseudorepresentation recognition; generic character recognition only; Hilbert irreducibility is proved by the arithmetic-properties node. Additional interface: Serre §7.2 Corollary 2 trace-zero density theorem for a non-CM modular λ-adic representation, or the general p-adic analytic Chebotarev/Haar-zero hypersurface theorem that implies it. Additional interface: Continuous semisimple recognition by good Frobenius traces.

Rankin's theorem for a classical newform f = Σa_nqⁿ of type (k, ε) on Γ₀(N) (Rankin 1939; Deligne–Serre 5.2 also cite Jacquet LN 278, Li and Ogg): Σ|a_n|²n^{−s} converges for Re s > k, and ζ(2s − 2k + 2)·Σ|a_n|²n^{−s} extends meromorphically to ℂ with a single pole, simple, at s = k. This is the classical specialisation of the GL₂ × GL₂ Rankin–Selberg integral. Additional interface: Holomorphy of the standard L-function of a cuspidal GL₂ representation under the stated twist, and nonvanishing of the finite-order Hecke-character L-value at the noncancellation point in Skinner p. 256. Additional interface: For cuspidal π on GL₂(A_F) and an algebraic Hecke character ψ, L(π ⊗ ψ, s) is entire; Hecke L-functions L(ψ, s) do not vanish at s = 1 + n, n ≥ 0, and ζ_F has a pole at 1.

Čebotarev's density theorem in Dirichlet density over ℚ: for a finite Galois extension M/ℚ and a conjugacy class C of Gal(M/ℚ), the unramified primes with Frobenius in C have Dirichlet density |C|/[M : ℚ]; in particular the primes that split completely in a Galois number field form an infinite set.

The upper Dirichlet density dens.sup X = limsup_{s→1⁺} Σ_{p∈X} p^{−s}/log(1/(s − 1)) of a set X of rational primes (Deligne–Serre (5.4.1)), with Σ_p p^{−s} = log(1/(s − 1)) + O(1), monotonicity and finite subadditivity.

Weight-one Eisenstein series with character and their Hecke eigenvalues: an Eisenstein eigenform of type (1, ε) on Γ₀(N) has a_p = χ₁(p) + χ₂(p) for p ∤ N, with Dirichlet characters satisfying χ₁χ₂ = ε (Hecke, Mathematische Werke p. 690, as cited in Deligne–Serre 8.1); and the Hecke-stable decomposition M₁(N, ε) = S₁(N, ε) ⊕ E₁(N, ε). Additional interface: For weights k≥2, the Hecke-stable cusp/Eisenstein decomposition and Eisenstein good-prime eigenvalue χ₁(q)+χ₂(q)q^{k−1}, with χ₁χ₂=ε, conductor and parity hypotheses; these give the two arithmetic character summands in Deligne–Serre Theorem 6.1.

Weight-two special-fibre Eichler–Shimura correspondence with Frobenius/Verschiebung components and the corrected ordinary versus supersingular subgroup-scheme fibres. Additional interface: The conventions (the model of X₁(N), the Picard or Albanese action of T_p and ⟨p⟩) under which an arithmetic Frobenius on V_ℓ(A_f) has characteristic polynomial X² − a_pX + ψ(p)p (Darmon–Diamond–Taylor Theorems 1.41 and 3.1(a)); a character of order at least three distinguishes ψ from its inverse.

Integral Fontaine–Laffaille comparison with coefficients and kernels for weights [0,k−1] inside [0,ℓ−2]; do not extend the proof to endpoint weights. Additional interface: Residual labelled tame-inertia characters for the regular Hilbert weights at sufficiently large unramified coefficient characteristic; inputs to Dimitrov §§2.12–2.13 and 3.1–3.2. Additional interface: The residual representation of a classical newform on inertia at ℓ for ℓ larger than the weight and prime to the level (fundamental characters of level one or two), as Ribet 1985 Theorem 2.1 uses it.

Wiles/Skinner–Wiles ordinary local shape (3.2), with exact subcharacter, unramified quotient, nebentypus/cyclotomic powers and hypotheses; imported by the attached-representation identification and the CM ordinary-line theorem. Additional interface: Ordinary good-prime filtration, unit-root quotient and exact graded characters; Hilbert version with labelled weights, nebentypus and specified cyclotomic powers. This roadmap owns the intersection with its fixed lattice and refinement comparison. Additional interface: The specified invariant ordinary line V_v,f with distinct graded characters in Dasgupta–Kakde §9.1; their exact ramified/unramified character hypotheses are needed. Additional interface: The exact ordinary inertia characters in KW II Corollary 7.8(i),(ii), under its residual irreducibility, unramified-base and norm-factor hypotheses.

Fine-level Kuga–Sato fibre powers, canonical equivariant smooth compactification/resolution and the boundary cohomology needed in Scholl §1.3; the ε-projector and its arithmetic application are owned here.

Kisin 2.7.6/2.7.7 fixed potentially semistable/crystalline inertial and Hodge-type quotient for any complete Noetherian local A° with a free continuous family, with finite-projective period module and coefficient specialisation. The universal pst-deformation-ring node alone is insufficient.

Period-ring D_pst, labelled Hodge–Tate grading, WD conversion and its dual/twist/normalisation functor laws for potentially semistable representations. Additional interface: Kisin's analytic continuation of crystalline periods in families (Kisin, Overconvergent modular forms and the Fontaine–Mazur conjecture, Invent. Math. 153 (2003), Proposition 5.14 and Corollary 5.15), for representations of G_{F_v} with φ replaced by φ^{f_v}, under the Sen-polynomial condition P(X) = XQ(X) with Q(0) not a zero divisor (Skinner footnote 9).

Generic proper smooth/semistable geometric comparisons, projectors, cohomological pull–push and coefficient change used by Scholl/Saito/Skinner; concrete eigenform applications stay in R19.5. Additional interface: Generic semistable/proper-smooth comparison compatible with finite-group and Hecke projectors; sufficient logarithmic compactification and coefficient-functor compatibility for Scholl/Saito realisations, not a theorem already asserting the modular conclusion. Additional interface: Faltings' de Rham and Hodge–Tate comparison for smooth projective varieties over p-adic fields, and the crystalline comparison at good reduction with Katz–Messing characteristic polynomials, applied to Shimura-curve, Kuga–Sato and Picard-modular-surface families.

Weight-two good-reduction crystalline representation from the p-divisible group of the modular abelian quotient; Barsotti–Tate equivalence in the stated coefficient conventions. Additional interface: The precise inertial/Hodge-type characterisation of weight-two potentially Barsotti–Tate lifts, including p=2 caveats; no extension of small-range Fontaine–Laffaille to weight p+1. Additional interface: The weight-two potentially Barsotti–Tate identification used in KW II Corollary 7.8(ii), with its norm-factor and local type hypotheses.

Generic Wach module existence for a crystalline lattice, exact weight convention, coefficient extension and semilinear basis-change laws; use wach-dcris-comparison for the reduction map. Repeated-root diagonalisation is not asserted.
Strong multiplicity one: the away-p finite component of a cohomological cuspidal GL₂ transfer determines its p-component; used in CDN Proposition 5.2.

Ribet level lowering at q|N for the weight-two squarefree-level trivial-character form when its absolutely irreducible residual representation is unramified at q, for sufficiently large coefficient characteristic.

Integral descent/interpolation of a degree-two determinant from an actual rank-two generic Hecke module over a finite flat complete coefficient algebra: closed integral traces, cross coefficients without 1/2, universal polynomial-law identities, finite quotients and continuity. Field-valued reduced points alone are insufficient. Additional interface: For the reduced O-flat KW algebra, descend the full determinant law from its actual product representation using integral traces/determinants and mixed coefficients; record continuity. This is an instance of generic interpolation, not Theorem B over an algebraic closure.

Use the existing modular-symbol rational structure, coefficient field, integral new Hecke algebra and ± period lines. Do not reconstruct or renormalise these upstream objects. For the weight-one sparse-eigenvalue proof, use the already specified sublayer8W inside this layer: Deligne–Serre Proposition2.7 integral-q-expansions-at-all-cusps finite-free Hecke-stable lattice, number field and algebraic-integral good-prime eigenvalues. This route precedes the Artin construction and is separate from the k≥2 modular-symbol proof; do not replan it in R15.2.

For Dirichlet characters χ, expand log L(χ,s) in the absolutely convergent Euler product for real s>1, and bound the prime-power terms with exponent m≥2 uniformly as s→1+. Combined with nonvanishing L(χ,1), this gives bounded nontrivial-character prime sums; with the zeta residue it gives the trivial-character prime-sum logarithm used in Deligne–Serre 8.4.

Use the existing conjugate-eigensystem construction over coefficient-field embeddings to obtain a weight-one eigenform with every good-prime eigenvalue σ(a_p). Layer8G imports the weight-one lattice from sublayer8W; use that branch and the existing eigenform/newform reduction when needed. Do not apply a discontinuous complex automorphism termwise to analytic functions or replan the upstream construction.

Classification of the irreducible unitary generic representations of GL₂(F_v): tempered (supercuspidal, twist of Steinberg, unitary principal series) or complementary series π(μψ, μ^{−1}ψ) with μ = |·|^t, 0 < t < 1/2 (Blasius §2.2).

The weight–monodromy conjecture for H² of smooth projective surfaces over p-adic fields (Rapoport–Zink Satz 2.13 with de Jong's alterations), and de Jong's integrality: the Frobenius eigenvalues on H^j of a smooth projective variety over a local field are integral Weil numbers of integral weight (Blasius Proposition 2).
Deligne's Weil I purity for smooth projective varieties with good reduction, applied to the Shimura-curve, Kuga–Sato and unitary realisations at unramified places.

Wintenberger's lifting of crystalline representations along central isogenies (Wintenberger, Invent. Math. 120 (1995), Theorem 1.1.3, Proposition 1.2, Remarks 1.1.4; Ann. Inst. Fourier 47 (1997), Theorem 2.2.2) for GL₂ → GL₂/{±1}: a crystalline representation of G_{F_v} into (GL₂/{±1})(Q̄_p) whose Hodge cocharacter lifts is the image of a crystalline GL₂-representation.

The geometric realisations used for Hilbert forms: (i) Blasius–Rogawski motives, in the cohomology of the PEL unitary Shimura varieties of Skinner §2.3.1 (GU(Φ), signature (2,1) at one place and (3,0) elsewhere) with good reduction at hyperspecial level above p, for a CM base-change twist of π; (ii) the three-dimensional ρ_Π of an essentially self-dual regular cuspidal Π on GL₃(A_F) with archimedean parameters as in Skinner (8), in an abelian scheme over a Picard modular surface, with WD(ρ_Π|D_v) ≅ Rec_v(Π_v) at good places (Skinner §2.3.3, after Blasius [B1, 4.1–4.6]). Only these early realisation exports are imported; the late rank-two comparisons AG2.5/late-gl2-modular-comparison and AG2.6/rank-two-comparison-with-r19, which consume R19, are not.

Unitary descent of the GL₂ and GL₃ parameters used by Skinner §2.3: the L-packet τ on U(2) with non-standard base change π_E ⊗ η|·|^{1/2} ([BR, Prop. 4.1.2]), the endoscopic packet on U(Φ) with d(σ_f) = 2 ([BR, Lem. 4.2.1]), and the GL₃ packet of Π = Sym²π ⊗ |·|^{−1}.

Group-independent eigenvariety gluing in Buzzard's form: Fredholm series of a compact U_p on orthonormalisable Banach modules over an affinoid weight disc, finite slope summands, and reduced affinoid pieces whose classical points are Zariski dense.

The instance for the totally definite quaternion algebra over a totally real F (Buzzard, Eigenvarieties §§8–11; Buzzard 2004 §7): overconvergent forms S^D_κ(U; m) over a weight disc with the action of T^S ⊗ U_p and classicality for slope small relative to the weight, as used in Skinner §2.4.2. L2 states the eigencurve over Q; the quaternionic instance over F is not yet stated by any layer.

sourceIssues.locator: Proposition 3.15 (p. 156), in its proof on p. 157; checked on the page image
sourceIssues.printed: For a geometric point s of M_n, the source identifies q_1^{-1}(s) with the order-p subgroups of E_s. It counts p + 1 of them when car(k(s)) ≠ p, but just one, namely the Frobenius kernel, when car(k(s)) = p.
sourceIssues.correction: In characteristic p the fibre has one point (the kernel of Frobenius) if E_s is supersingular and two points (the kernel of Frobenius and the étale subgroup of order p) if E_s is ordinary.
sourceIssues.reason: For ordinary E_s over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, E_s[p] ≅ μ_p × Z/p has exactly two subgroup schemes of order p. Deligne's own Proposition 4.3 (p. 162) says that for a p-isogeny between curves with invertible Hasse invariant either its kernel or the kernel of its dual is étale, and the special fibre of M_{n,p} has two components (F and V). The proposition itself (representability and properness) and the degree p + 1 away from p are not affected.
searched: Numdam copy of Séminaire Bourbaki 11 (1968/69), exposé 355 (the Lecture Notes 179 text)

review.reason: Confirmed on the page image of printed p. 157: the fibre of q_1 over a geometric point of characteristic p is said to have a single element, which fails for ordinary curves (two subgroup schemes of order p, connected and étale). The sentence is in the proof paragraph of Proposition 3.15; the proposition itself and the degree p + 1 away from p are unaffected, so the effect is recorded as on the proof.

sourceIssues.printed: Entry [53] credits Takeshi Saito with a preprint entitled Modular forms and p-adic Hodge theory, identified by math.AG/0612077.

sourceIssues.reason: arXiv:math/0612077 is titled "Hilbert modular forms and p-adic Hodge theory" and is listed under math.NT; "Modular forms and p-adic Hodge theory" is Saito's 1997 Inventiones paper on elliptic modular forms. Lemma 7.7 concerns Hilbert modular forms, so the preprint is the intended reference.

the published Invent. Math. 178 (2009) bibliography was not seen

sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 2.4, p. 24, and §3.3, p. 30 (arXiv v2); checked on the page images
sourceIssues.printed: Theorem 2.4 on p. 24 chooses integers satisfying N ≥ 3 and k ≥ 2, then defines S_N = {ℓ ∤ Nk!}. On p. 30 the category is PM^{S′}_ℚ, using S′ = { p | p ∤ N′k! }.
sourceIssues.correction: S_N = {ℓ : ℓ | Nk!} and S′ = {p : p | N′k!}, the sets of excluded primes.
sourceIssues.reason: In PM^S the set S is where no crystalline realisation or integral comparison is required (§1.2, p. 9), and the comparison isomorphisms are established exactly for ℓ ∤ Nk! (p. 30 and Proposition 5.6). The source itself defines S = S_N by the primes dividing Nk! (p. 13) and S′ by the primes dividing N′k! (p. 27); the printed sets are their complements.
sourceIssues.known: new: present in arXiv v2 (11 Dec 2025), the latest version; the Ann. Sci. ÉNS 2004 text is organised differently and has no Theorem 2.4
searched: Ann. Sci. ÉNS 37 (2004), Numdam copy (SHA-256 385dc212…): no counterpart of Theorem 2.4; its §2 defines S as containing the primes dividing Nk!

review.reason: Confirmed in arXiv v2: p. 24 (Theorem 2.4) and p. 30 print the sets with ℓ ∤ Nk! and p ∤ N′k!, while pp. 9, 13 and 27 define S by the primes dividing Nk!. Scoped to arXiv v2.

sourceIssues.locator: §1, p. 241 (definition of infinity type (k, w)) against Theorem 1, p. 242 (Hodge–Tate type) and §2.4.1, p. 251; published Documenta text
sourceIssues.printed: The source specifies x ↦ sgn(x)^{k_i}|x|^{−w} for the central character on p. 241. On p. 242 it places the nonzero degrees at (w − k_{i(j)})/2 as well as (w + k_{i(j)} − 2)/2. In §2.4 it takes w = 2, with Rec_i(π_i)|C^× ≅ (z̄/z)^{1/2} ⊕ (z/z̄)^{1/2}.
sourceIssues.correction: With the central-character convention of §1, the representation of equation (1) has D_HT non-zero in degrees (w − k_i + 2)/2 and (w + k_i)/2. The printed degrees are right when π_i has central character sgn(x)^{k_i}|x|^{2−w}, which is how §2.4 uses w (its 'w = 2' has trivial central character on R_{>0}).
sourceIssues.reason: Skinner's own dictionary in §2.3.3 sends z^a z̄^b in Rec_i to D_HT-degree −a (checked on GL₁: |·|^{−1} ↦ (zz̄)^{−1} ↦ degree 1, the inverse cyclotomic character). For π_i with Blattner parameter k and central character sgn^k|x|^{−w}, Rec_i(π_i ⊗ |·|^{−1/2})|C^× = z^{−(w+k)/2} z̄^{−(w−k+2)/2} ⊕ (conjugate), giving degrees (w+k)/2 and (w−k+2)/2. Test: for the unitary π_E of an elliptic curve (k = 2, trivial central character, so w = 0), (1) and the trace identity T_x(frob_w) = x∘φ(char(GL₂(O_w)diag(ϖ_w,1)GL₂(O_w))) of §2.4.2 give H¹_ét(E_Q̄, Q_p), with degrees 0 and 1, while the printed formula gives −1 and 0.
searched: EMS Press article page for Documenta Math. 14 (2009) 241–258 (no erratum or correction listed; accessed 2026-10-07)
arXiv listing for C. Skinner with 'Hilbert' in the title (no preprint version found)

review.reason: Confirmed in the published text: p. 241 gives the central character sgn(x)^{k_i}|x|^{−w}; p. 242 the degrees (w − k)/2 and (w + k − 2)/2; §2.3.3 (p. 251) reads degrees −a, −b off the archimedean parameter; §2.4 (pp. 251–252) takes w = 2 with unitary archimedean parameters and obtains degrees 0, 1. With the convention of p. 241 an elliptic curve has w = 0 and degrees 0 and 1, so the printed degrees are those for central character |x|^{2−w}. Nothing in the proofs is affected.

sourceIssues.locator: Remark at the end of §2.4.2, p. 256; published Documenta text
sourceIssues.printed: From the identity L(π ⊗ ψ₂^{−1}, s − 1/2) = L(ψ₁/ψ₂, s)ζ_F(s) and L(ψ₁/ψ₂, 1) ≠ 0 the Remark concludes that L(π ⊗ ψ₂^{−1}, s) has a pole at s = 1.
sourceIssues.correction: The pole is that of L(π ⊗ ψ₂^{−1}, s − 1/2) at s = 1, that is, of L(π ⊗ ψ₂^{−1}, s) at s = 1/2.
sourceIssues.reason: ζ_F has its pole at s = 1 and L(ψ₁/ψ₂, 1) ≠ 0, so the right-hand side, hence L(π ⊗ ψ₂^{−1}, s − 1/2), has a pole at s = 1; substituting s + 1/2 for s places the pole of L(π ⊗ ψ₂^{−1}, s) at 1/2. For an elliptic curve E and trivial ψ₂ the left side is L(E, s) in the motivic variable. The contradiction with cuspidality, an entire L-function, is unaffected.
searched: EMS Press article page for Documenta Math. 14 (2009) 241–258 (no correction listed)
web search for an erratum to the article, 2026-10-08 (none found)

review.reason: Checked at p. 256: the identity is written with s − 1/2 on the left, so the pole at s = 1 is one of L(π ⊗ ψ₂^{−1}, s − 1/2). The argument is unaffected.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 7.2 and its proof, case (i), pp. 60–61 (authors' final version, 30 May 2009; the published Invent. Math. 178 text was not seen)
sourceIssues.printed: For p > 2 the proof deduces that the unramified character γ_{v,f}, a square root of ψ_v with ρ_f|D_v of the form (χ_pγ_{v,f} ∗; 0 γ_{v,f}), does not depend on f from the single fact that the residual representation of the forms in the localisation at m does not depend on f.
sourceIssues.correction: The deduction needs, for v ∈ Σ not above p, that N(v) ≢ −1 mod p or that ρ̄_m|D_v is not a direct sum of two unramified characters; otherwise the Hecke algebra has to be enlarged by the operator of a uniformiser of D_v^×, or the lemma stated for each of its eigenvalues.
sourceIssues.reason: The two candidates are γ and γη, η the unramified quadratic character. Their residual semisimplifications are {χ̄_pγ̄, γ̄} and {χ̄_pγ̄η̄, γ̄η̄}. Since p > 2, η̄ ≠ 1, and the two sets coincide exactly when χ̄_p|D_v = η̄, that is when v ∤ p and N(v) ≡ −1 mod p. Then a split ρ̄_m|D_v ≅ γ̄ ⊕ γ̄η̄ is compatible with both candidates, while a non-split one still singles out γ̄ as its unramified quotient. The Hecke algebra of the lemma contains only the operators at places outside S ⊇ Σ, so the maximal ideal does not see the sign. Whether forms of both signs actually occur in one localisation (as level raising suggests when N(v) ≡ −1 mod p) was not decided.
searched: web search for an erratum or corrigendum to Serre's modularity conjecture (II), 2026-10-08 (none found)
the authors' final version on Khare's UCLA page; the published Inventiones text was not seen

review.reason: Checked at pp. 60–61 of the authors' final version: case (i) of the proof consists of the one sentence on the independence of the residual representation. The elementary computation in the reason shows that this does not determine γ_v when v ∤ p, N(v) ≡ −1 mod p and ρ̄_m|D_v is a sum of two unramified characters. Recorded as a gap in the proof, scoped to this version; the statement is not asserted to be false.

reviewHistory.notes: Independent review of revision round 2 (BP-AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations~2), following the review REV-AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations, which did not accept the plan. All five corrections that review asked for were checked and are made: one global object ρ_{π,λ} with a normalisation dictionary; purity outside Saito's scope (Blasius); the reader synchronised; the R34.6 dependency; Skinner's inputs named. All 66 nodes were checked against the 26 public sources (hashes reproduced), every one of the 13 baseline declarations was read at the pinned commits, and the eleven handed red-team findings were checked. 21 nodes verified, 45 corrected in place, none added, none unverifiable. Principal corrections: (1) dictionary clause (g) and the two Skinner–Wiles nodes: Skinner–Wiles send uniformisers to arithmetic Frobenius elements, so their representation is σ_λ(π)^∨ = ρ_{π,λ} ⊗ ε_ℓ, not Carayol's σ_λ(π); a clause (j) for Khare–Wintenberger added. (2) R19.1/newform-rank-two-realisation: Diamond–Flach–Guo's M_g is the conjugate form's realisation; the roadmap's M_g is its twist by M_{ψ^{−1}}, which corrects the determinant for characters of order above two. (3) Carayol nodes: the determinant argument (5.5), the reversed kernel in the Picard–Lefschetz statement and its request, the local fundamental representation, and the case 𝔭 = v of Theorem (A), which needs global irreducibility; the global object now depends on Theorem (B) only, so Theorem (A) can use the irreducibility node. (4) CM definition: the inducing character α is not algebraic, α|·|^{−1/2} is. (5) Khare–Wintenberger's sign lemma: a hypothesis added for N(v) ≡ −1 mod p, with source issue E6 and a gap. (6) Closure: the λ-adic characters of algebraic Hecke characters and the converse for Hodge–Tate characters are imported from their existing owners (AG2.0/galois-character-of-an-algebraic-hecke-character, R24.5/character-system) instead of being requested from R01.1; a spurious prerequisite R34.6 of the Eichler–Shimura node removed; missing direct prerequisites added. (7) Source issues E1–E4 confirmed; E5 and E6 added. The reader's section on mistakes quoted the sources verbatim and is regenerated in the roadmap's own words; short quotations removed from the packet. Reader document and suggested file brought in line with every correction; check_blueprint reports no errors, and the suggested file elaborates at the pinned Mathlib with no warning other than the expected placeholder ones. The plan is accepted as one complete target-level pass: all six layers are planned, none closed, with 12 gaps and 51 supplier requests recorded.
